extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, processors, importers, exporters of new chemical substances; regulated entities, industry stakeholders, and legal/regulatory advisors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for preparing comments and complying with EPA proposed Significant New Use Rules (SNURs) for specific new chemical substances under TSCA, including submission procedures, required information, and specified protective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: TSCA section 5(a)(2) significant new use determination factors
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining that a use is a 'significant new use,' EPA must consider all relevant factors, including: the projected volume of manufacturing and processing; the extent to which a use changes the type or form of exposure of human beings or the environment; the extent to which a use increases the magnitude and duration of exposure of human beings or the environment; and the reasonably anticipated manner and methods of manufacturing, processing, distribution in commerce, and disposal of the chemical substance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA considered toxicity, potential human exposures, and environmental releases in the context of these four factors when identifying significant new uses for the substances in this rule. These four enumerated factors are the controlling analytic framework for determining whether a use is a significant new use under TSCA section 5(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: SNUN notification timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons must notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any chemical substance for an activity designated as a significant new use in the SNUR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 90-day SNUN initiates EPA's evaluation; manufacture/processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has reviewed the SNUN, made an appropriate determination, and taken any required regulatory actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNUN submission form and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: SNUNs must be submitted on EPA Form No. 7710-25, generated using e-PMN software, and submitted in accordance with procedures in 40 CFR 720.40 and 721.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-PMN software is available electronically at EPA's new chemicals review page. Follow the regulatory submission procedures; failure to use required forms or channels may render a submission noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to include in SNUNs and testing expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters are required to provide information in their possession or control and to describe other information known to or reasonably ascertainable by them; TSCA section 5 does not generally require generation of new test data unless a TSCA section 4 rule/order requires it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a TSCA section 4 rule/order requires testing, that information must accompany the SNUN. EPA has authority to require appropriate testing upon review and encourages early consultation about protocol selection and use of alternative test methods (NAMs) under TSCA section 4(h). Providing detailed human exposure and environmental release information improves EPA's ability to evaluate SNUNs; submitting no test data may increase likelihood EPA will take action under TSCA sections 5(e) or 5(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) handling and 40 CFR 721.11 procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit CBI to EPA through email or Regulations.gov; if including CBI, follow EPA docket instructions, clearly mark claimed CBI, and follow confidentiality procedures in 40 CFR parts 2 and 703. EPA has a 40 CFR 721.11 procedure for identifying confidential significant new uses upon demonstration of bona fide intent to manufacture or process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent a final determination on a confidentiality claim, EPA is required to keep claimed information confidential. Manufacturers/processors can combine the bona fide submission under 40 CFR 721.11 into a single step when the chemical identity and significant new uses are both CBI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability: entities subject to SNURs
rubrics_metrics.description: SNURs apply to persons who manufacture, process, or use the chemical substances; importers and exporters may also be subject under TSCA sections 12(b) (export notification) and 13 (import certification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA provides NAICS code examples (e.g., 325, 324110) to help entities determine applicability but notes the list is not exhaustive. Importers must follow applicable TSCA import/export regulations (40 CFR part 707 and related Customs regulations) and certify compliance with TSCA rules and orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated cutoff date for determining ongoing uses
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA designates April 24, 2026 as the cutoff date for determining whether a new use is ongoing for the chemical substances in this proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses that began on or after the cutoff date would have to cease upon the effective date of the final rule and may only resume after complying with SNUR notification requirements and EPA action. EPA explains the cutoff selection in Unit II.E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use limited to manufacture of batteries
rubrics_metrics.description: For the listed PMN substances, no use is allowed other than in the manufacture of batteries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SNUR designates as a significant new use any use other than manufacture of batteries; this extends the protective measures of underlying TSCA Orders to all manufacturers/processors, not just the PMN submitters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Battery labeling requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Batteries or packaging containing multiple batteries must have exterior labeling indicating they contain substances subject to TSCA restrictions (example label text provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label placement: directly on the visible exterior of wrappings/packaging for sale, shipment, or storage; unpackaged batteries must be labeled or tagged on visible exterior surface; labels must be durable to equal/exceed battery life and cannot be removable without defacing/destroying; repackaging must maintain or replace visible label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dust control requirement (99% capture/control efficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacture, processing (including recycling/reclaiming), or use of the substance is permitted only with dust controls that achieve an overall minimum combined capture and control efficiency of 99%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All processing includes recycling or reclaiming from batteries or other items; failure to implement 99% dust control is designated a significant new use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Air release property-boundary limit
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a significant new use to release the substance to air at a single site such that the rolling average concentration over 14 days at the property boundary exceeds 1.3E-4 mg/m^3 for the substance individually or in aggregate with other cobalt-containing MMO substances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This numeric aggregate limit is carried from the TSCA Orders and is used to determine whether an activity constitutes a significant new use for purposes of the SNUR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing/processing time limitation and related conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacture or processing of the PMN substance is not allowed for more than one year unless there is no air release of the substance or the air release limit is updated, and likewise not allowed for more than one year unless there is no inhalation exposure to the PMN substance or the Respiratory Protection Limits are updated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-year limit reflects the Orders' temporary authorizations and the need for updated exposure information or revised limits to continue longer-term operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposal restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a significant new use to dispose of the substance or waste streams containing the substance other than by hazardous waste landfill in compliance with RCRA Subtitle C or incineration if the incinerator ash is disposed of by hazardous waste landfill in compliance with RCRA Subtitle C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibits land disposal or other disposal routes inconsistent with Subtitle C hazardous waste controls; noncompliant disposal is a significant new use requiring SNUN.

rubrics_metrics.name: No release to water
rubrics_metrics.description: The SNUR designates any release of the PMN substance to water as a significant new use unless it conforms to specified requirements (see §721.90 references).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA identified aquatic toxicity concerns and lists aquatic toxicity testing as potentially useful information; release to water is explicitly constrained as part of the protective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respiratory protection requirements and APF thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to worker exposure monitoring, use a NIOSH-certified respirator with APF ≥ 1,000 where inhalation exposure potential exists; once monitoring is complete, require respirators according to specified 8-hour TWA thresholds and corresponding minimum APFs (detailed numeric breakpoints provided). If 8-hour TWA exceeds 5.3E+00 mg/m^3, manufacturing/processing/use must cease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: APF below 50 is permitted only when the PMN substance contains ≤ 3% cobalt by weight. The numeric TWA ranges and corresponding APFs are precisely enumerated in the regulatory text and must be used to set respiratory protection programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal protective equipment (PPE) and engineering/administrative controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of personal protective equipment is required where there is potential for dermal exposure, and engineering and administrative control measures (e.g., enclosure, local ventilation, workplace policies) must be considered and implemented to prevent exposure where feasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of determining reasonably likely exposed persons, employers should consider and implement engineering/administrative controls before relying solely on PPE; these control hierarchies are specified by reference to §721.63(a) provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hazard communication program and required hazard statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a hazard communication program including health and environmental precautionary statements on each label and in the Safety Data Sheet (SDS); for these substances EPA specifies potential hazards: carcinogenicity, genetic toxicity, skin sensitization, respiratory sensitization, reproductive toxicity, neurotoxicity, and specific target organ toxicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements specified in §721.72 subsections apply; alternative hazard/warning statements meeting GHS and OSHA Hazard Communication Standard criteria may be used. The program must ensure adequate communication throughout manufacture, processing, distribution, and disposal activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers, importers, and processors of these substances must comply with recordkeeping requirements as specified in §721.125(a) through (k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart A provisions apply except as modified; records must be maintained consistent with §721.125 to demonstrate compliance and support EPA oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation or revocation of certain notification requirements (§721.185 applicability)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of §721.185 (limitation or revocation of certain notification requirements) apply to these sections as specified in the regulatory text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA may limit or revoke notification requirements under conditions set out in §721.185; consult that provision for processes and criteria for such actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General SNUR provisions and equivalence to PMN requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons subject to SNURs must comply with the same requirements and EPA regulatory procedures as PMN submitters under TSCA section 5(a)(1)(A), including information submission requirements of TSCA sections 5(b) and 5(d)(1), authorized exemptions (TSCA 5(h) provisions), and the regulations at 40 CFR part 720. User fee provisions appear in 40 CFR part 700.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SNUR submitters should be familiar with PMN procedural obligations and exemptions; noncompliant submissions may be subject to regulatory action. SNUN submissions trigger the same analytical and procedural framework used for new chemical reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tips for preparing comments and public comment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments are public and will be posted online after EPA review; do not submit CBI via email or Regulations.gov; follow EPA instructions for CBI and commenting; see EPA commenting tips and alternative ways to comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments received may be redacted or withheld by EPA. The docket contains further instructions and alternative submission methods (e.g., Regulations.gov, mail) and commenters are encouraged to review 'Tips for Preparing Your Comments' in Unit I.E.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potentially useful information for SNUN submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA identifies certain information as potentially useful to support an Order modification request or an SNUN: e.g., aquatic toxicity testing results and detailed information about human exposure and environmental release that may result from the significant new use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not necessarily required, providing such data can support modification of Orders and improve EPA's evaluation. EPA strongly encourages early consultation to determine appropriate tests and approaches, including NAMs to reduce vertebrate testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic impact and user fee structure
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's economic estimates: estimated cost per SNUN submission approximately $45,496 for large business submitters and $14,976 for small business submitters; user fee generally $37,000 but reduced to $6,480 for qualifying small businesses; estimated export notification per-notice cost ≈ $106.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These estimates include preparation/submission costs, CDX registration, and user fees. EPA's prior experience shows relatively few SNUNs are received annually; small business fee relief is available and may materially reduce reporting costs for qualifying firms. See docket economic analysis for details.
